summary: Reviewer DESIGN. I read the frozen runtime (train/workflow/runner/controls/heads/metrics/selection/provenance/execution), the archived A1 JSON, the protocol section 4.4, the 21/11 entries of decisioni.md and the registry, and ran two small CPU prototypes with the unmodified modules (D0/D1 composition on the test fixtures; the embedding with extra probes). D0 is feasible exactly as GPT describes: all five learning rates have best and current paired states with the stated counters, y/y*/masks/thresholds/partition replay bit-for-bit from calibration.pt through existing functions, and the scoring function already supports the clean target on any index set; but every input lives only on Leonardo, so D0 is a Slurm job needing an ID, a budget line and a registered decision, and the epoch-150 state can be reproduced only against a pooled published value. D1 is mechanically sound (same initialisation, batch orders and dropout masks are achievable exactly; noisy-held selection tracks the clean held error to within 1-2 points of recovery) and compares the TCN like for like with cleanLS, but its outcome table is not decidable, a pass at the 150-epoch boundary falls in two rows, and its most likely outcome (row 1 or an intermediate gain, my judgement) does not support the declared follow-up. The follow-up "one variant frozen once, then the original control repeated" is a post-hoc specification change on the same seeds, folds and held halves, with no fresh world and no stop rule: not protected against circularity. The constructive proof is correct and uses the unmodified head with LayerNorm in the path, but it holds only in eval mode: with dropout active the embedded weights are far from a stationary point. I found no issue that blocks scientific convergence on D0; the items below are preconditions before any launch and before D1 is read.

findings.title: D0 and D1 need a registered decision of Simone, a budget line and logical IDs before any launch; the document never says so
findings.location: docs/reviews/pose_temponet_temporal_diagnosis_20261121.md sections 5 and 7; docs/pose_temponet_frozen_protocol_20261117.md lines 104, 158, 186, 219; docs/decisioni.md last entry of 21/11
findings.claim: The protocol makes a new diagnosis after a failed gate conditional on a registered decision. What is registered today is the gate failure and GPT's proposal as REVIEW_REQUIRED, quoting a request of Simone for an analysis and a review prompt. No authorisation to run D0/D1, no budget attribution, no ID and no frozen reading rule are registered, and the diagnosis only says that allocations and budget will be published before release. D0 is not a local step: it is a cluster job.
findings.evidence: Protocol line 186: "La riserva copre avvii/sforamenti contabilizzati, non retry. [...] Una nuova diagnosi/ripartenza richiede decisione registrata."; line 104: "Eventuale modifica della specifica richiede decisione registrata."; line 158: "Un esito negativo dei gate torna alla decisione pertinente, non autorizza mutazioni."; line 219: "Superamento tetti, cambio scientifico o retry richiedono nuova decisione". decisioni.md 21/11: "Arresto scientifico prescritto, non attesa di autorizzazione." and the entry "Diagnosi TCN: seguito proposto, REVIEW_REQUIRED" quoting Simone: "perché la TCN non passa il controllo temporale? Analizza cosa non funziona e come possiamo risolverlo, poi preparami il prompt per farlo rivedere a claude". execution.py: every job carries "retry": "forbidden_without_new_decision" and the graph is frozen (validate_graph). Inputs of D0 exist only on Leonardo: selection_states.pt 18,386,382 bytes, two calibration.pt 228,630,380 and 228,396,140 bytes, train cache 474,412,856 bytes (plan_controls.json .inputs.cache_train), target_reference_train and pose_stats on $SCRATCH; no copy on the Mac (searched ~/wearusfm_local and the repo).
findings.suggested_fix: State in the diagnosis and in decisioni.md that D0 and D1 are launched only after a decision of Simone registered there, with: logical IDs, walltime and resources, cost in GPU-hours and local hours, the sub-budget charged and its residual (A1 consumed 3.681111 GPUh of the 56.1 authorised for the planned matrix, which does not cover new tests), and the reading rule of DESIGN-2 committed before the fits. Review convergence is not that decision.

findings.title: D1 outcome table is not decidable: overlapping rows, undefined terms, no precedence
findings.location: docs/reviews/pose_temponet_temporal_diagnosis_20261121.md section 5, table of four rows and the paragraph before it
findings.claim: A pass at the 150-epoch boundary satisfies row 1 (recovery >= 50% in three panels) and row 3 ("curve ancora in discesa/bordo") at once, with opposite consequences. "Molto inferiore" (row 2) and "scarso rispetto al riferimento pulito" (row 3) have no quantity and the fitting reference is not named (cleanLS on y*, or zero). Every intermediate outcome (for example 35-49% without a large fitting/held gap) falls in row 4 with no consequence. A noise-free regression at constant learning rate is expected to be still descending at 150 epochs, so the boundary clause will fire for a reason unrelated to an optimisation defect. With one seed and a table that will steer a specification change, the reading would be post hoc.
findings.evidence: Row 3 text: "Anche il fitting pulito resta scarso rispetto al riferimento pulito, o curve ancora in discesa/bordo"; closing sentence: "Le righe qualitative non sono nuovi gate numerici"; D1 text: "Se la lettura resta ambigua o a bordo a 150, esito diagnostico inconclusivo". In A1 the selected epoch was 31 of 150 because of noise (selection_temporal_TCN_post.json .selected.exposure = 31.0; E_dyn at 150 = 0.7415560124949256): that early optimum has no reason to hold without noise. Fitting-side references needed for a decidable rule already exist in the archive: cleanLS on fitting 0.708654 / 0.749626 (calibration_{0,1}.json .outer_reference_statistics.linear_diagnostics.L0.temporal_margin_clean_fit_statistics), oracle on fitting 0.654332 / 0.693246 (reconstructed from L13 recovery 0.270896 / 0.199309).
findings.suggested_fix: Freeze before the fits a rule built on the same 50% arithmetic, with precedence: (1) held recovery at the noisy-MSE-selected checkpoint in fold0, fold1 and pooled; if >= 0.50 everywhere it is row 1 whatever the position of the minimum; (2) otherwise fitting-side recovery (E_cleanLS,fit - E_TCN,fit)/(E_cleanLS,fit - E_oracle,fit), with the fitting oracle computed directly rather than reconstructed: >= 0.50 with held < 0.50 is row 2, < 0.50 is row 3; (3) a minimum in epochs 146-150 only qualifies a failure as unresolved horizon. State that a failure at lr 0.003 / 150 epochs chosen under noise is ambiguous, while a pass holds a fortiori.

findings.title: The most likely D1 outcome does not support the declared follow-up; attainability under noise stays unmeasured
findings.claim: Row 1 would show that architecture, optimiser and 20 users suffice without noise. It cannot show that a more parsimonious or more regularised variant reaches 50% when trained on y, nor that 50% is attainable under this noise with about 920 windows. The archive bounds what a smaller noise price can give: about 7-8 points of margin, against 26-31 missing. The remaining points must come from learning the non-linear temporal part better under noise, which neither A1, D0 nor D1 measures. The single allowed variant would therefore be chosen blind, and its failure would again be ambiguous between a poor variant and a gate that is not attainable at this noise and sample size.
findings.evidence: Linear world (a=0, sigma=1.35; selection_linear_TCN_post.json, calibration_{0,1}.json .outer_reference_statistics.linear), held E_dyn: oracle 0.722484 / 0.763721, ridge 0.729602 / 0.770106, TCN 0.733731 / 0.774719. With no temporal signal the TCN recipe ends 0.011247 / 0.010998 above the oracle = 19.7% / 18.7% of the temporal margin (0.056981 / 0.058817); the closed-form ridge 12.5% / 10.9%. Temporal world: TCN is 0.043206 / 0.047715 above the oracle. Approximate additive reading: signal captured about 44% / 38%, noise price about 20% / 19%, net 24.17% / 18.88%. Baseline asymmetry: closed-form WLS L0 fitted on y is behind cleanLS by 19.1% / 16.4% of the margin, neural L0 by 13.6% / 10.8%, so the 50% gate equals 56.0% / 54.9% of the distance from the best noisy-trained linear reader to the oracle (TCN: 33.2% / 26.8%). L13 fitted on the clean target recovers in-sample only 27.09% / 19.93% (linear_diagnostics.L13.temporal_margin_recovery_fitting), and fitted on y it is 85.6% / 69.5% of the margin behind cleanLS: the gate requires the non-linear part.
findings.suggested_fix: Before D1 is read, register the decision tree: for each row which options are admissible (one recipe variant, a re-specified control, or stop), how many further attempts (one) and what happens if the variant fails. If the recipe route is wanted, add one pre-declared attainability reference on the noisy target (for instance the same driver with a parsimonious or well-specified student, explicitly a reference and not a candidate), or record that the variant is chosen without evidence of attainability. Report in the diagnosis the decomposition above.

findings.title: The follow-up "one variant frozen once, then the original control repeated" is not protected against circularity
findings.claim: Changing the candidate after a failed gate and repeating the gate is a specification change made after seeing this world. The generator and noise seeds are hard-coded, the folds are the same two alternating halves, and the same held halves have already chosen learning rate and epoch in A1, would be read again by D0 and D1, and would then confirm the variant. The proposal bounds the search to one variant in words, but declares no fresh world, no fresh noise, and no stop rule.
findings.evidence: controls.py:141 `base_seed = 20261118 + 1000*outer_fold` (teacher L), +1 (T), line 185 `window_noise(base_seed+2, ...)`. A1 read the held halves at 5 learning rates x 154-304 checkpoints (selection_temporal_TCN_post.json .curves: 304, 154, 154, 154, 154 points). Protocol line 106: "gli stessi held outer scelgono LR/epoca e giudicano recupero, quindi la qualifica è ottimista"; line 104: "nessuna etichetta scientifica negativa o ricerca finché si vince". Section 6 of the diagnosis: "scelta e congelata una sola volta prima di ripetere il controllo originale". A fresh world is cheap: each WLS calibration took 391.3 s and 392.9 s on 8 CPUs (receipts TCNH-wls-calibration-{0,1}-20261120.json .details.elapsed_seconds).
findings.suggested_fix: Register, before D1 results exist: the variant is evaluated on the original world (for comparison with A1) and on one fresh world with pre-declared generator and noise seeds and its own calibration; the 50% must hold on the fresh world; no re-draw of worlds; a single attempt; if it fails the line returns to Simone. Changing the seed constant touches the frozen runtime, so it needs its own source identity and review.

findings.title: D1 needs a new driver; require a parity gate proving that the target is the only change
findings.claim: The training target and the selection target are bound to the same field, and the frozen search cannot run one learning rate with a fixed horizon, so D1 cannot be obtained by configuration. It can be composed from the unmodified classes outside the frozen tree, which keeps the frozen source identity. Because the claim of D1 is that only the target changes, the new driver must first reproduce A1 when given the noisy target.
findings.evidence: workflow.py:236-239 builds the training set from `bundle.targets[fold][indices]`; the evaluator at line 298 scores `_metric_panel(bundle, fold, rows)` which reads `bundle.targets` too. train.py:542-560 loops over `selection.INITIAL_LRS`, extends automatically through `needs_epoch_extension` and adds an edge learning rate. provenance.py:236-248 `source_manifest` covers scripts/pose_temponet/**, so a new file there changes source_sha256 9aaf1c8b.... My CPU prototype with the unmodified modules (Trajectory + PairedCandidate.advance(initial_epochs) + a training set built from `bundle.clean_targets`) printed: "D1 same init: True | same batch orders: True | same dropout RNG end state: True | same shuffle RNG end state: True" and "composed noisy path == frozen curve: True".
findings.suggested_fix: Implement D0 and D1 as an external driver importing the frozen checkout unchanged, with explicit pins of the old artifacts. Add a mechanical gate before the clean fits: the driver run with target y reproduces the first published checkpoints of lr 0.003 (pooled MSE and E_dyn from selection_temporal_TCN_post.json .curves) at 1e-12 on the pinned GPU context; record initial_sha256 50fb2294... and the per-epoch epoch_order_sha256 of both runs. Extra evaluations must stay inside eval mode so that they draw no random number.

findings.title: D0 reproduction is underspecified: epoch 150 has only a pooled published value, no tolerance, device not stated
findings.claim: "Prima riproduce gli score rumorosi pubblicati, rispettivamente del selezionato e del punto 150" can be done per fold only for the selected checkpoint. For the final state only the pooled curve point exists. The comparison tolerance and the device are not stated, and restoring a state through the frozen class requires the original device type and numeric profile.
findings.evidence: Selected checkpoint: full sums archived per fold in .selected_outer_statistics, .selected_outer_clean_statistics, .selected_fitting_diagnostics. Final state: only .curves[lr=0.003].points[-1] = {mse 1.8521482905919395, edyn 0.7415560124949256, fold_steps [4350, 4500]}; the job log has 920 selection_checkpoint events, all pooled. In-run check used np.isclose(atol=1e-12, rtol=1e-12) in the same GPU process. Trajectory.restore compares device_type and numerical_profile() (torch 2.2.0a0+git6c8c5ad, 8 threads, CUBLAS :4096:8) and raises "trajectory provenance/recipe mismatch" otherwise.
findings.suggested_fix: Write in the package: per-fold reproduction for the selected state, pooled-only for epoch 150; tolerance 1e-12 on one GPU with the pinned numeric context (numeric_sha256 12cb2a0b...), or a declared looser tolerance if a CPU re-score is chosen; assert the rebuilt bundle manifest equals the archived .bundle (bundle_sha256, target_sha256, clean_target_sha256, thresholds 0.5437424309221641 / 0.5374366720436082) before any score; compute the fitting oracle directly instead of the algebraic reconstruction.

findings.title: D0 leaves free information unused: all 20 saved states and the per-epoch training losses
findings.claim: The diagnosis says the fold-separated fitting curves are missing. They are missing from the JSON, but each saved current state carries the whole per-epoch training-loss history of its fold, for all five learning rates. All 20 saved states can be scored on both halves and both targets for a few seconds each, which turns two points into a ten-point picture (learning rate x selected/final) with no selection consequence.
findings.evidence: Trajectory.state() includes "epoch_losses" (one record per completed epoch: loss_sum, window_count) and PairedCandidate.state() stores best_states and current_states for every learning rate; `_run_search` line 556 keeps `states[lr]` for all of them. Benchmark: one held evaluation including the clean score takes 1.352 / 1.371 s per fold (TCNH-gpu-benchmark-20261120.json .details.benchmark.cells.TCN_post.fold{0,1}.statistics.eval.median). File size 18,386,382 bytes = 20 states x 905,805 bytes (benchmark checkpoint_file_bytes) plus metadata.
findings.suggested_fix: In D0 export epoch_losses of all current states (train-mode loss on y, per fold) and score all 20 states on fitting and held against y and y*, reproducing first the published pooled best and final points of each learning rate. Declare them descriptive.

findings.title: D1 cost: the proportional 0.205 GPU-h is about 1.6 times too low for the design described, and the cleanLS-on-y* score is not costed
findings.claim: GPT states that 0.205 GPU-h is not a preventive. For the package: an evaluation costs more than a training epoch, and D1 doubles the evaluations (fitting and held, both targets at each checkpoint). The descriptive comparison with cleanLS fitted on y* and scored on y* needs the closed-form WLS L0 to be refitted, because calibration.pt holds components and statistics, not predictions.
findings.evidence: Benchmark medians per fold-epoch: train 1.166 / 1.168 s, held evaluation including the clean score 1.352 / 1.371 s. (1.17 + 1.36 + 1.33) s x 300 fold-epochs is about 1,160 s = 0.32 GPU-h before start-up, reading two 228 MB calibration.pt and the 474 MB cache, quarter-epoch points, the parity gate and margin. GPT's arithmetic is right: 59 updates per epoch, 8,850 updates, 4,427 s x 150/900 = 738 s. controls.py:573 computes the clean prediction with `factor.predict_mixture(held, {"L": 1., "T": a}, 0.)` and scores it only on y.
findings.suggested_fix: Budget D0 + parity gate + D1 together from the benchmark p95 values with the protocol's factor 2 (order of 1 GPU-h, to be measured), and include the WLS L0 refit in float64 with its own reproduction check (0.710431 / 0.749920 on held first).

findings.title: The fitting/held gap, called the main clue, has the size expected from noise memorisation and does not indicate poor cross-user generalisation
findings.claim: GPT hedges this correctly and proposes D0 for it. The archive already shows that the noise-free linear fit transfers to the other 20 users without loss, and that the TCN gap sits between those of the two closed-form readers fitted on y. The gap is therefore uninformative about generalisation of the learned function; the clean fitting error of D0 is what decides.
findings.evidence: Fitting to held change of E_dyn on y (fold0 / fold1): oracle -0.0009 / -0.0021; cleanLS +0.0018 / +0.0003; WLS L0 fitted on y +0.0156 / +0.0137; WLS L13 fitted on y +0.0919 / +0.0822; TCN +0.0348 / +0.0282, about 2.2 times the 385-feature WLS and 0.36 times L13. GPT's apparent fitting recovery reproduced: 86.12% / 69.25%.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword section 1: the gap is compatible with noise memorisation alone; add the comparison with the WLS gaps and the absence of a gap for cleanLS.

findings.title: Selecting the epoch on noisy held MSE while training on y* is sensible, and D1 is like for like with cleanLS
findings.claim: On the held half the noisy score equals the clean error plus the noise term up to a small cross term, so the frozen selector tracks the clean held error and keeps the gate arithmetic identical. D1 uses the original denominators. A clean-trained TCN is compared with a baseline that was also fitted on the clean target, so D1 removes both the linear-part and the temporal-part noise cost: it is not a one-factor change relative to what the gate measures, and its 50% is an easier, different quantity. The held half stays both selector and judge, with a bias of the order of the cross term.
findings.evidence: Cross term of the TCN at the selected checkpoint, oracle_sse + clean_sse - noisy_sse: +2,915.8 = +1.6% of the margin SSE 182,695.6 (fold0); -817.3 = -0.5% of 158,738.3 (fold1). Denominators: 0.056981 / 0.058817 / pooled 0.057820. Clean scale: TCN held clean E_dyn 0.127856 / 0.154431; cleanLS about 0.165 / 0.192; the 50% gate corresponds to about 0.083 / 0.096.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the selector as proposed. State in the document that D1's recovery is like for like with cleanLS and therefore not comparable point for point with A1's 24.17% / 18.88%.

findings.title: The constructive proof holds only in eval mode: with dropout active the embedded weights are far from a stationary point
findings.claim: The proof is correct and has no shortcut: unmodified head from heads.make_head, target from controls.generate_components and synthetic_target, normalisation and the factor a absorbed in the head's own output layer and affine branch, LayerNorm at its initial values and inside the path, comparison on all 160 steps and on the central crop. It shows that the candidate can represent y* at inference. It does not show that this function is compatible with the frozen training objective. This also confounds row 3 of D1: a clean fitting residual can come from dropout and weight decay, not from an optimisation defect.
findings.evidence: My re-derivation: eval rmse_central 5.004e-07, max 6.405e-06 (fold0) and 5.021e-07, 4.354e-06 (fold1), equal to GPT's JSON; LayerNorm gamma x 1.1 gives rmse 1.180e-01. Train mode, same weights: error variance 0.813 (fold0) and 0.599 (fold1) of var(a*T); loss / gradient norm at the embedded point 2.5e-13 / 1.6e-07 in eval against 1.117e-01 / 6.0e-01 with dropout. Most redundant exact embedding (8 copies in the 64-wide layers, 4 in the 32-wide, eval rmse 5.9e-07): train-mode error still 0.146 / 0.106 of var(a*T). Inputs are 8 windows of Gaussian noise and the teachers are regenerated on torch 2.14, while the real controls used torch 2.2.0a0 and their generator hashes are inside `components`, which calibration.json drops.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the claim as "representable at inference". Add that the embedding is not a fixed point of the recipe with dropout 0.1 and weight decay 0.01, and have D1 publish the train-mode loss (epoch_losses) next to the eval-mode fitting error so that a dropout-limited fit is not read as an optimisation failure.

findings.title: A priori the most likely D1 outcome is row 1 or an intermediate gain; D1 is still worth its cost as an exclusion test only
findings.claim: This is my judgement, not a measurement: I ran no learnability simulation because the real latents are only on Leonardo. The noisy-trained TCN is already not far from the clean level the gate implies, and the linear part transfers across users without a gap, so a clean-trained TCN probably improves substantially. Rows 2 and 3 are less likely but would redirect the work completely, which is what justifies a run of about 0.3 GPU-h. Under row 1 the run confirms what the diagnosis already believes and leaves the choice between a recipe variant and a re-specified control open.
findings.evidence: Noisy-trained TCN held clean E_dyn 0.127856 / 0.154431 against about 0.083 / 0.096 needed for 50%; cleanLS fitting to held gap +0.0018 / +0.0003. Not verified by simulation.
findings.suggested_fix: Run D0 first and publish it; keep D1 with the decidable rule of DESIGN-2 and the registered decision tree of DESIGN-3, so that the expected outcome has a pre-declared consequence.

Receipt .artifacts.states: selection_states.pt, 18,386,382 bytes, sha256 f9f4d4ad1a59f117b05d8ed411daeefb2bef68709f611f368e379e65a1e1bbf0, on $WORK.

No cluster access, no job, no push. `git status --short` in the review checkout returns 0 lines; my work directory wf3_design_work was deleted with its full literal path; no reviewer process left running. Notes at /Users/simonebenatti/wearusfm_local/tcn_temporal_diag_review/design_notes.md.
